title: Restriction to a slice Grothendieck site preserves injective abelian sheaves
statement: Let C be a small category and J a Grothendieck topology as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with sheafification for abelian groups on C and on C/W. For every W in C, the restriction functor J.overPullback AddCommGrpCat W preserves injective objects. No existence of pullbacks in C, precoverage presentation, or HasExt is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 03F3 (1); its proof invokes Modules on Sites, Lemmas 03DI and 03DJ

proof.text: For a slice sheaf G, construct the presheaf at V as the direct sum of G(V → W) over all arrows V → W. Restriction sends the φ summand through G into the a ≫ φ summand. Sheafify. Sheafification adjunction and the direct-sum universal property identify maps from this sheaf to F with maps G → F|W, naturally on both sides. Thus this is a left adjoint to restriction. This argument works for sieves without pullbacks in C.

Monomorphisms of slice sheaves are sectionwise injective because their kernels are computed sectionwise. Direct sums preserve these injections, even for empty index sets. Exact sheafification preserves the resulting monomorphism, so the constructed left adjoint preserves monomorphisms.

For a monomorphism A → B in the slice and a map A → I|W, transpose across the adjunction. Extend the resulting map from the extension of A to I across the monomorphism to the extension of B, using injectivity of I. Transpose back. Naturality of the adjunction gives the required extension to B, proving that I|W is injective.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 03F3 (1), with the direct-sum construction and monomorphism argument of Modules on Sites 03DI--03DJ spelled out
